instruction.name: fldgt.s
instruction.description: Floating-point bound-checked load, condition rj > rk.

cases.name: base operand through an ALU operation

experiment.command: ./bench --method slope --unroll 800 --unroll2 1600 --iters 40 --warmup 10 --reps 5 --init 'addi.d $r20, $sp, -1024; li.d $r22, -64; and $r20, $r20, $r22; li.d $r4, 8; st.w $r4, $r20, 0; li.d $r4, 0; st.w $r4, $r20, 8; li.d $r5, 0; addi.d $r4, $r20, 0' --asm 'fldgt.s $f0, $r4, $r0; movfr2gr.s $r4, $f0; add.d $r4, $r4, $r20'

./bench --method slope --unroll 800 --unroll2 1600 --iters 40 --warmup 10 --reps 5 --init 'addi.d $r20, $sp, -1024; li.d $r22, -64; and $r20, $r20, $r22; li.d $r4, 8; st.w $r4, $r20, 0; li.d $r4, 0; st.w $r4, $r20, 8; li.d $r5, 0; li.d $r4, 0' --asm 'fldgt.s $f0, $r20, $r4; movfr2gr.s $r4, $f0'

experiments.command: ./bench --method slope --unroll 800 --unroll2 1600 --iters 40 --warmup 10 --reps 5 --init 'addi.d $r20, $sp, -1024; li.d $r22, -64; and $r20, $r20, $r22; li.d $r4, 8; st.w $r4, $r20, 0; li.d $r4, 0; st.w $r4, $r20, 8; li.d $r5, 0; addi.d $r4, $r20, 0' --asm 'fldgt.s $f0, $r4, $r0; movfr2gr.s $r4, $f0; add.d $r4, $r4, $r20'
experiments.name: base operand path

latencies.notes: 5 cycles from the base operand rj to the destination. The loop closes through movfr2gr (2 cycles) and, because the loaded value has to be turned back into an address, through an add.d (1 cycle); the chain also carries one further cycle that the address generator pays whenever the address comes from an ALU operation rather than straight from the register file, so 4 cycles are subtracted. The load itself is 5, the same as fld.d/fld.s and one cycle above the integer loads.

experiments.name: index/bound operand path

latencies.notes: 5 cycles from the index or bound operand rk to the destination. Where the loaded value can feed the address or the range check directly the chain is just the load plus movfr2gr (2 cycles); when an andi or add.d is in the path the chain carries one more cycle than that helper, which is the ALU-address premium rather than load latency.

throughput.name: 8 independent addresses
throughput.asm: fldgt.s $f0, $r21, $r30; fldgt.s $f1, $r23, $r30; fldgt.s $f2, $r24, $r30; fldgt.s $f3, $r25, $r30; fldgt.s $f4, $r26, $r30; fldgt.s $f5, $r27, $r30; fldgt.s $f6, $r28, $r30; fldgt.s $f7, $r29, $r30
throughput.init: addi.d $r20, $sp, -1024; addi.d $r21, $r20, 0; addi.d $r23, $r20, 8; addi.d $r24, $r20, 16; addi.d $r25, $r20, 24; addi.d $r26, $r20, 32; addi.d $r27, $r20, 40; addi.d $r28, $r20, 48; addi.d $r29, $r20, 56; addi.d $r30, $r20, -8; li.d $r4, 0x3ff0000000000000; movgr2fr.d $f0, $r4; movgr2fr.d $f1, $r4; movgr2fr.d $f2, $r4; movgr2fr.d $f3, $r4; movgr2fr.d $f4, $r4; movgr2fr.d $f5, $r4; movgr2fr.d $f6, $r4; movgr2fr.d $f7, $r4
throughput.command: ./bench --unroll 1000 --iters 1000 --warmup 10 --reps 5 --core 0 --init 'addi.d $r20, $sp, -1024; addi.d $r21, $r20, 0; addi.d $r23, $r20, 8; addi.d $r24, $r20, 16; addi.d $r25, $r20, 24; addi.d $r26, $r20, 32; addi.d $r27, $r20, 40; addi.d $r28, $r20, 48; addi.d $r29, $r20, 56; addi.d $r30, $r20, -8; li.d $r4, 0x3ff0000000000000; movgr2fr.d $f0, $r4; movgr2fr.d $f1, $r4; movgr2fr.d $f2, $r4; movgr2fr.d $f3, $r4; movgr2fr.d $f4, $r4; movgr2fr.d $f5, $r4; movgr2fr.d $f6, $r4; movgr2fr.d $f7, $r4' --asm 'fldgt.s $f0, $r21, $r30; fldgt.s $f1, $r23, $r30; fldgt.s $f2, $r24, $r30; fldgt.s $f3, $r25, $r30; fldgt.s $f4, $r26, $r30; fldgt.s $f5, $r27, $r30; fldgt.s $f6, $r28, $r30; fldgt.s $f7, $r29, $r30'
throughput.notes: 8 independent lanes: 7.98 core cycles per 8 instructions, CPI 1. Slope method (--unroll 1000, --unroll2 2000).

notes: Latency measured per source operand on LA464: 5 cycles from the base operand rj and 5 cycles from the index or bound operand rk. The chains close through movfr2gr (2 cycles) and, where the value has to be combined with the base or kept above the bound, through an add.d or andi as well; the extra cycle those chains show beyond the helper is the ALU-address premium, not load latency. The 64-byte-aligned buffer holds 8 and 0 so the chase stays inside one cache line.
